title: Rafi's Wiggling Seeds
markdown:
Sun popped. Sky bright pink and orange. Rafi bounced. Science club day! He dashed to the kitchen. Plum the rabbit twitched. Mr. Reed hummed. Breakfast smells.

“Morning! We plant seeds! Help them grow!”

Reed brought a big clear jar. “Special seeds. Tiny promises. We’ll help them wake up.”

Rafi beamed. A pinch of seeds, tiny pebbles. He put a few on soil in the jar. Plum nudged more with her nose. They peered in. Sleeping seeds. Brown specks. Rafi poked the soil. “Awake yet?” No sprout.

Plum tilted her head. “Sleepy. Like a nap.”

Rafi frowned. He wanted sprouts now. He watched Reed water a plant. A sunbeam splashed. “Hmm. Seeds need water? And sunshine for energy?”

He picked up the jar, added a tiny dribble of water, then set it where the sunbeam danced. He and Plum sat, eyes glued. Suddenly — a tiny movement. A seed gave a little shimmy. Then another.

“Plum! Look! They’re wiggling!”

Whiskers twitched. “They are!” She did a happy jump that shook the table, then sat very still so she would not shake the jar.

A little green tip poked out, pushing through the soil. Another followed. Tiny worms stretching awake. Rafi clapped. A big grin. “They’re waking up!”

Reed rumbled: seeds need a drink, like cereal, and sunshine for energy, like play. Science. Not magic.

Rafi nodded at the tiny green sprouts. A powerful feeling bubbled. “We helped them grow.”

Plum twitched. “They look happy now.”

He marked the jar with a grease-pencil line so tomorrow’s bigger sprouts would have something to beat, and left the sunbeam on duty. Plum guarded the jar from further table-jumps, which was a serious job for a rabbit.
